convoLines.text: "Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."

"Here's the thing: There's a laugh I keep hearing in my head — not anyone here, just from before. Sometimes I borrow it. I'll be hauling water and laugh at nothing, and for a second it's like the old world left the door open a crack."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Gerald owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Grace grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Grace is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I keep turning over the last thing Gerald said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Nobody says Gerald's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About this wound — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Since Gerald died... I keep expecting to see Gerald at the fire. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — ...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on the talking-to-strangers part. That's my read."
"The System gave different things to different people. That's not random — it's matchmaking. It's building a team."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"Sure. I'll be around."

"Never mind this wound — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."

deathBeat: d30: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Gerald Das is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d30: 🕯️ Gerald Das is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d30: The village's quarrel was with Gerald — and Gerald is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d32: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Hummice is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d31: That night, they bring Gerald home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d30: At the grave, Joshua, Balnur, Grace and 2 more speak for Connor — "Gerald trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d30: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
d30: 📺 SYSTEM: "SEASON FINALE APPROACHES! Party cap raised to FIVE! Go out with a BANG! (Figuratively. Mostly.)"
burialWindowSay: d30: The village's quarrel was with Gerald — and Gerald is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d30: At the grave, Joshua, Balnur, Grace and 2 more speak for Connor — "Gerald trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d31: That night, they bring Gerald home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d32: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+2 integration)
d33: You say a few words for Gerald. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d33: You bury Gerald. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d33: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+2 integration)
echoSample: d33: "Huh. Let me think about that." "Gerald owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d33: "I keep turning over the last thing Gerald said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d33: "Nobody says Gerald's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d33: "Since Gerald died... I keep expecting to see Gerald at the fire. Stupid."
d37: "Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Gerald always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d37: "Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Gerald is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
echoV2Sample: d33: The village raises a marker by the fire — Gerald, day 33. the wild. A place to stand.
echoV2DeltaSample: d33: The village raises a marker by the fire — Gerald, day 33. the wild. A place to stand.
halfRationLines: d84: "Half rations for three days, voted and held — or a hard hunt now, hungry, to fill the bins before it's choosing-who-eats."
d93: "Triage tents and broth for the sick, or half rations till it passes, or the healthy hunt hard to keep everyone fed. Pick — everything costs."
